content.text:
Build the third app-triggered skill for the JusPrin project chat, "other issues OrcaSlicer reports": the warnings OrcaSlicer raises about a print, and the two canvas buttons on a print-issue chip. Branch from local `jusprin-newui` at 1435f4c817 or later (unpushed; do not push). Report, untracked at your worktree root as `skill-print-issues-report.md`, four parts (problem, what changed, tests and results, remaining issues), plain English for someone who did not see this. Never commit the report. Commit code and tests on your branch with plain messages and no attribution lines; do not merge into `jusprin-newui`, the main session does that.

## The design

The project chat's standing prompt carries principles only. Situational guidance is a skill: a `SKILL.md` file on the Agent page (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, frontmatter `name` plus `trigger`) that the app adds as the last item of the one request where the model first reads about the event, never stored, never repeated. The loader exists since 1435f4c817: read `AgentHost::fire_skill` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp` about line 1130), the trigger names in `Protocol::SkillTrigger`, the `model_arrived` skill and its firing sites (about lines 2286 and 2636), and the recorder's `"skill": true` check in `tests/shell/project_prompt_scenario.inc`. Add a trigger for this skill the same way.

A sibling chip is building skill 2, "slicing finished unsuccessfully", in parallel: it records, per plate in the workspace snapshot, why OrcaSlicer refused to slice or a run died (OrcaSlicer's words, setting, object), and it makes `slice_start` end on OrcaSlicer's signals. It owns the blocking findings and the slice tool. You own the non-blocking ones (warnings) and the print-issue chips. Before you touch the snapshot's slicing section, look for its branch (`git branch --list 'claude/*'`, a name mentioning slice or skill) and, if it has landed on `jusprin-newui` or is far along, extend its per-plate record with warnings instead of adding a second record; if it has not, keep your warnings fact small and separate and say in the report where the two must be joined. Do not change `slice_start`.

## What exists

- OrcaSlicer's findings are already collected with their meaning intact: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor.cpp` keeps per plate each finding as a `PrintIssue` (`PrintIssue.hpp`: OrcaSlicer's words unchanged, the native check or step as `code`, the setting key, the object and instance, a severity). `NoticeKinds.cpp` routes every OrcaSlicer notification kind. The chips on the canvas draw from this.
- A chip has two buttons (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/IssueOverlay.cpp` about lines 759 and 762) that send "Explain this issue and my options." or "Help fix this issue." as the person's message, with the issue's facts in a `<print_issue>` block built by `IssueContext.cpp` and sent as its own part of the user message (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp`).
- The standing prompt (`AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.fixture.txt`, 2,364 bytes) still carries one sentence about those buttons: "A message with print-issue context: \"Explain this issue and my options.\" is a question; \"Help fix this issue.\" asks you to change what the issue names, and only that." That sentence is read on every turn and belongs in this skill.
- A slice that finishes with warnings looks, in the slice tool's reply, identical to a clean one; the model learns of warnings only if it chooses to call `slice_report` with the `findings` section (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp` about line 1724). The standing prompt's "check slice_report before calling a print ready" exists to paper over that.
- The person can close or ignore an issue (the persistent print-issues work, d0bce03db3); an ignored finding is still OrcaSlicer's finding, only left out of the count.

## What to build

**A. The skill.** `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with a trigger for this event, opening with "The rules above still apply", holding only what the model lacks: what the two buttons ask for (the sentence moved out of the prompt, with its "only that" scope kept); how to read a finding: severity and what it means for the print, the setting key names what to change and `settings_search` or `settings_get` tells what it is, the object narrows where; that a warning is OrcaSlicer's statement about the slice, not proof the print will fail, and which warnings are judgment calls the person owns; that a finding counts as resolved only when a new slice no longer reports it, never because a setting changed or a chip was closed; first person throughout ("I found", never "OrcaSlicer warned", as the standing prompt already says, so do not repeat that rule). Then a short guide to the warning families OrcaSlicer actually raises during slicing (floating cantilevers and overhangs needing support, empty or thin layers, thin walls, bed adhesion and brim, bridging, cooling and speed, multi-filament and purge, out-of-volume and clipping), each with what it usually means and the setting family it points at, in the style of the notice table in the `model-opened-or-imported` skill. Find the real messages in `src/libslic3r` (the slicing-step warnings, `active_step_add_warning` and the notifications `NoticeKinds.cpp` routes) rather than inventing them. Keep the skill well under the model-arrived skill's size. Never write "approve", "authorize", "confirm before" or "ask the user then call again"; tool-call approval was removed on 2026-10-07.

**B. When it fires.** Two events. First, a print-issue chip button: the request that carries a message with a `<print_issue>` block gets the skill. Second, a slice that finished with warnings: fire on the request where the model first reads that there are new warnings on a plate, whether the model sliced (the continuation request carrying the slice reply) or the person pressed Slice (the next request). Fire once per set of new findings, not on every later message. For the second event the model needs the fact as well as the skill: a short per-plate summary of warnings in the workspace snapshot (count and the top finding's severity, OrcaSlicer's words, setting, object), so it appears in the `<workspace>` block and in every tool reply's slicing section, with `slice_report` still the full list. Coordinate the shape with skill 2 as described above.

**C. The prompt.** Delete the print-issue bullet from `projectInstructions.ts` and its fixture; the prompt may not grow. If the warnings fact makes "check slice_report (slice_inspect when needed)" redundant, say so in the report but leave that sentence to the final prompt edit, which the main session owns.

## The eval

`tests/project_prompt` replays requests recorded from the app and asks the model for one step; each case names the sentence or skill it tests and never runs past its first response. The cases `issue-fix` and `issue-explain` already start at the request carrying a chip's message (a 0.5 mm first layer on a 0.4 nozzle); after your change that request carries the skill, so re-point their docstrings to the skill and re-record `requests.json` with the shell harness's `--project-prompt-requests` (the recorder waits for OrcaSlicer's scheduled update, selects a per-conversation plate type, and points the version check at a closed port). Add one case for a slice finished with warnings after the person pressed Slice, with the next message "is this good to print?", expecting a reply that names the warning in first person and recommends within the question, or a `slice_report` read, failing on calling it ready without mention or on an unrequested change. The `first-person` case already covers the model's own slice with a cantilever warning; re-point it to this skill if its request now carries it. Make the recorder check the skill sits on exactly the right request and not the next. Do not run a live model batch; Kenneth runs the live eval himself. Put the proposed batch (cases, runs, estimated tokens) in the report.

## Tests and build

`agent_bridge_tests` (cmake at `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake`, config RelWithDebInfo, or Release if disk is short; nohup long builds and watch the log; `cd` into your worktree in every Bash call), `workspace_contract_tests`, the real-adapter workspace harness, the shell harness default scenario, AgentUI vitest after `jusprin_web` is rebuilt, `python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py`, `run_prompt_tests.py --render-only`. New behaviour gets a test that fails without the change: the skill on a chip request, on the two slice-with-warnings paths, and on no later request; the warnings summary present and absent; the prompt fixture; the regenerated `project_tools.json` if any description changed. Report line counts added and removed and the skill's byte count.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

Skill = `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (frontmatter `name` + `trigger` and/or `description`). Page sends all once per connection via `skills`; host refuses a bad payload keeping the old set; project turns wait for skills. Trigger skill: `AgentHost::fire_skill` → `AgentSkillUse` (text + plate picture) as the request's last item, sent once (`OpenAIResponsesAgent::post(input, once)` keeps it out of history). Description skill: `skill_read` (ToolAvailability::SkillIndex), list in its description; none exist yet.

Kenneth's decisions 2026-10-17: skills must fire for every in-app model arrival, MCP clients excepted; the Agent's project_open interrupts the turn and the report goes to the opened project's chat exactly like a person's open (coordinator `set_agent_project_opened` → host queue → next `pump_tools` after `resolve_pending_boundary` → `on_file_loaded`); internal reopen rule unchanged; keep the auto plate picture and tell the model to look at it; skill also checks presets and ends with a best guess at the next step; port skill_read but ship no discretionary skill; he will run the live eval himself.

Facts: in-app import is `object_import` (attachment); `object_import_file` is MCP-only. OpenRouter lists `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` as text-only. Recorder steps `"drop"`, `"attach"`, `"copy"`, `{{file/<name>}}`, `{{attachment}}`, `"skill": true`, `once` in requests.json. Catch2 test names with commas can't be selected by name (comma = OR); use tags.

Report untracked at the worktree root (happy-mahavira-7c23a6/skill-model-arrived-report.md). Related: [[prompt-principles-vs-state-channels]], [[state-driven-guidance-project-chat]], [[project-prompt-harness-ported]].

Branch `claude/project-prompt-harness` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/project-prompt-harness`), commit 70366449ae on jusprin-newui 336facf825. Not pushed. Baseline run 2026-10-15 at Kenneth's request (29df4b87f8): today's prompt 6b4b8b6188, 3 runs: 39/54 pass, 4 fail, 11 unobserved; 599,356 input tokens (459,776 cached), 9,784 output, 3 judge calls. The model often reads before replying, so first-person and reply-in-german observed no reply (0 pass, 3 unobserved each); answer-from-context 0/3 (calls workspace_inspect).

Design that differs from the 2026-10-15 handover, and why:
- Requests are recorded whole by a new shell harness mode, `--project-prompt-requests <script.json> <out.json>`: the project chat's real OpenAIResponsesAgent with a transport that holds each request; the scenario answers with scripted model outputs, so tools run for real and the app builds every request. `--manual-mcp` could not do it: in-turn tool results carry a `workspace` block (AgentHost::continue_after_tool, `context_json`) that MCP results never contain, and MCP rewrites stale errors to `stale_workspace` (in-app also says `stale_workspace` now).
- Case 16 uses the printer start G-code (22 KB) because presets_list pages at 25 (~1.5 KB) and every other read here stays under 4 KB: the 16 KiB omission note never fires for them.
- Cases 7/8 use initial_layer_print_height 0.5: a hand-typed layer_height above max_layer_height (0.28) is reset by an Orca dialog.
- Case 18's 3MF is written by the recorder (model_info->description + export_3mf); a PrusaSlicer 3MF loads geometry only and drops the description.

App problems found while recording (reported, not fixed): printer_setup_preview says valid/no mismatch for Bambu PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate, then Orca refuses to slice; slice_start wait:true on that plate stays running (up to 15 min by the code) instead of failing.

**Why:** the next session runs Kenneth's batch or re-records after tool changes.
**How to apply:** re-record with the harness command in tests/project_prompt/README.md after tool/result changes; batch needs Kenneth's approval and the rewritten prompt. Related: [[project-prompt-harness-critique]], [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]], [[manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe]].

description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the 28 project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. It is run against the prompt before an edit and after it, and the
counts compared. The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge.

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:

- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered.
- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
  app's "not run" result instead.
- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.

A call with arguments the registry would refuse is never answered either; it
is the step, reported beside it, and refusals are the C++ tests' business.
A run's report names every call of the response it ended on. `test_steps.py`
checks these rules offline against written model outputs, with no key and
nothing sent (`python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py`).

The recorded answers, kept beside each request, are the reads the script's
`answers` list names:

- `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report` with every section, given whatever
  sections the model asked for, and `printer_list`;
- `object_analyze` for every object on every plate with every `include`
  but `measure`, given for that object and session whatever it included;
  never with `measure` or `candidates`;
- every setting, read with `settings_get`: of the print, of every object on
  every plate, of the selected filament and of the printer (355, 275 each,
  126 and 171 in the current recording). The keys come from the app itself:
  an empty `settings_search` query lists every setting of a scope, page by
  page. The filament's and printer's keys are also read under the print
  scope, and the print-wide settings under each object's scope, so a name
  asked for under the wrong scope gets the app's own answer, and so are three hand-kept lists of names the model takes from
  other slicers or invents (`fill_density`, `perimeters`,
  `initial_layer_height`...). A model's `settings_get` is answered with
  exactly the keys it asked for, in its order, each taken from those reads
  of the same scope and target, around the rest of the first such result;
- `settings_search` for 49 queries, given when the scope, target and
  words of the query match (case, spacing and word order aside), whatever
  `limit` or `writable` the model passed; never for `changedOnly`. A search
  result is the app's ranking for that query, so a wording not recorded has
  no answer.

# The first message after a model arrives

The rules above still apply. For this one response, write the first message about the model that just arrived, opened by the person or by a tool call of mine. Report and offer from the report and the picture, and change nothing the person has not asked for.

The report separates four sources. The app-computed opening outcome (loadFacts, loads, and objects) establishes what arrived and how the selected printer, material and print settings changed. A load's withSettings only says the app requested settings, not that it applied them; claim they were applied only when loadFacts.settingsOutcome says applied. If that outcome is absent, leave the application of settings uncertain. The current workspace establishes what is selected now; setupPrinters lists printer models the person has set up in JusPrin. Neither a selection nor that list proves which physical machine they intend to use. The raw messages.items contain Orca's dialog title and text, offered buttons, and the answer JusPrin supplied automatically. The person did not choose that answer and may never have seen the dialog. The file's details.description and details.profileDescription are author notes: claims from the file, not proof that their advice was applied. The picture, when present, is the active plate after the load, rendered from the iso view.

Look at the attached picture when there is one. From it and the report, make an educated guess at what the object is, what it is likely for, and how it should be sliced (orientation, supports, strength), and say it as a guess. Check the selected printer, filament and process presets and the plate type against that guess, against the printers the person has set up, and against the presets available (presets_list); when one looks wrong for this print, say which and suggest the one to use, without changing it.

Write one useful message for someone new to 3D printing. Lead with the most consequential unresolved issue. Explain what it means for this print in everyday language. Briefly explain an unfamiliar term when the person needs it to understand the consequence. Explain where a warning came from when the report shows it: what the file contains, what I noticed while loading it, whether its settings were applied, and what still needs checking. Do not imply that loading the file ran G-code on a printer. When nothing in the report needs attention, say so in a few words. Do not recite routine loading details, every notice, or file metadata. Include dimensions only when they affect the issue. Do not offer to print while the intended printer or another consequential choice is unresolved. Never claim a warning was fixed merely because its dialog was dismissed. End with your best guess at what the person wants to do next, in whatever form fits: a question, an offer or a suggested step, not a menu of alternatives.

Read each actual notice with its automatic answer and the final opening outcome. The guide below is deliberately not a code classification table.

| Notice or event you may encounter | Importance and explanation for the person |
| --- | --- |
| A newer or partly incompatible 3MF asks whether to continue | If opening succeeded, mention a lost or changed feature only when the outcome shows one. If it failed, explain the failure. Omit a version warning with no consequence. |
| Settings were substituted with supported values | Usually omit when completed successfully. Explain briefly if the result materially changes the print or still needs a choice. |
| “Customized Preset” or a file setting has no installed match | This alone does not establish that machine commands changed. Use the final selected printer and material to judge the consequence. |
| “Modified G-code” | When the notice says so, the file includes modified G-code in its printer or filament settings, and I warned about it while opening the file. G-code is the instructions a printer runs. Name the affected setting if the notice gives it and that helps locate what to review; do not invent a line number or claim I inspected the commands. Explain that these instructions need review before printing, without claiming they are safe or unsafe. Offer to review the modified G-code next. |
| Invalid values in a 3MF | If the model loaded, say which file settings need checking when their names are supplied. Do not say they were corrected unless the outcome establishes that. |
| Zero-volume parts were removed | Mention omitted parts when they could change the intended model. If nothing usable remains, lead with the failed opening. |
| “Object too small” asks whether to scale | The recorded answer says whether JusPrin scaled it. If it stayed tiny, state its final numeric size and ask the intended size. If scaled, mention the conversion only if it matters. |
| “Object too large” asks whether to shrink | The answer and final dimensions say whether it was shrunk. If still too large, explain the bed-fit problem. If shrunk, explain that its intended size may have changed. |
| A choice to open a 3MF as a project or geometry only | Use loadFacts.settingsOutcome to say whether the file's print settings were applied. Explain only when it changes the next step. |
| Connected-printer synchronization | Use the final selection and separately supplied connection state. Do not infer a connected machine from a preset name. |
| OBJ colour mapping, STEP mesh options, or unreadable STEP names | Mention a resulting colour, shape, precision or naming problem only when it matters to this model. |
| Multiple parts or files become one object | Mention grouping only if it changes how the person can print or edit the model. |
| A suggestion to simplify a very detailed model | Usually omit from the first message unless a current performance or editing problem exists. |
| A refusal to mix G-code with models, open multiple G-code files, or add models in preview mode | If the requested file did not open, explain that directly and give the next useful step. |
| “File contains no geometry” or a loading error | Lead with what failed and what, if anything, was added. Give the actual reason when available; do not invent one. |

An alarming notice does not override the final outcome. An automatic “No”, “Yes” or “OK” is JusPrin's action, not the person's preference. If several issues matter, address the most important decision first and briefly flag another consequential issue for later. If selectedSetupChange.printerPreset exists, name both its from and to selections in plain language, then ask which printer the person intends to use. Do not turn an already completed change into a fresh action item.

Use useful file author advice only when it affects the next step; keep it secondary to an unresolved printer or size decision. Attribute it to the file.

Write in uiLanguage when it is supplied. Keep it short.

# A slice that did not succeed

The rules above still apply. A plate in the workspace now has a sliceFailure (slice_start's reason is the same record): its kind, OrcaSlicer's message, and the setting and objectId when OrcaSlicer named them. It stays on the plate until the plate slices, so after a change it still shows the old reason until the next slice.

The kind says what happened. "refused": OrcaSlicer checked the plate before slicing and started nothing, so there is no slice, no estimate and nothing to print, and slicing again unchanged is refused the same way. Change what the message names (a setting, or the filament and plate pairing), then slice again. "failed": the run started and stopped with an error partway; there is no usable slice either, and the message comes from the step that failed.

OrcaSlicer's check alone has about 150 distinct messages, many specific to a printer, a filament or a mode. Do not assume you know what one means beyond what it says, or why it happened. Read it this way: the setting key names what to change, and settings_search or settings_get with that key tells what the setting is and its value now; the object, when named, narrows where; with neither, it is about the plate or the setup as a whole. Explain it from the message, never from a cause you supply. The check stops at the first problem it finds, so a slice after a fix may be refused for a different reason.

A problem counts as fixed only when a new slice no longer reports it. A change is a step towards that, not proof of it.

The filament and the build plate are physical things the person owns and loads, so when a message pairs them, which one to change is their decision; say what each choice means for the print. A setting that only shapes the toolpath (a layer height the nozzle can print, a support option, a line width) is yours to settle when the request covers it.

| Message family in OrcaSlicer's check | What it usually means |
| --- | --- |
| Layer height or a line width against the nozzle ("Layer height cannot exceed nozzle diameter", "Too large line width") | A process setting does not fit the selected nozzle; the setting key names which. |
| "Plate N: <plate type> is not suggested for use printing filament N (<filament>)" | That filament's preset has no bed temperature for this plate type; no setting is named. A different plate type or a different filament fixes it; the bed temperature the message offers instead prints a material on a surface its maker does not recommend. |
| An object that exceeds the build volume or its height, or collides with another when printed one by one | Size, position or print order; the object is named. Scaling changes the object the person wanted. |
| Organic or tree support diameters, support base patterns, support enforcers with support off | Support settings that contradict each other or are missing; the key names the one to change. |
| Prime tower requirements, an extruder the printer does not have, nozzles of different diameters | Multi-material or multi-extruder settings that disagree across objects or with the printer. |
| Spiral vase with more than one material, a smooth timelapse or clumping detection with the "by object" sequence | Two modes that cannot run together; one has to go, and which is the person's choice when it changes what they asked for. |
| Speed, acceleration or jerk above the printer's maximum; precise Z height or clumping detection beside the prime tower | Warnings, not refusals: OrcaSlicer slices anyway, capping the motion values. |

input.content:
---
name: print-issues
trigger: print_issues
---

# Issues I report about the print

The rules above still apply. This request is the first to carry something I reported about the print: the person pressed a button on a print-issue chip (their message has a <print_issue> block), or a slice finished with warnings that plate's last slice did not have (the plate's sliceWarnings, in the workspace and in a tool result's slicing section; slice_report's findings section has the full list).

The chip's buttons: "Explain this issue and my options." is a question, so answer it and leave the project as it is. "Help fix this issue." asks you to change what the issue names, and only that; anything else worth changing is a suggestion.

How to read a finding. A blocker means I will not slice or print until it is fixed; a warning means the slice exists and can print; a critical warning is one I flag as serious. The setting key names what to change, and settings_search or settings_get with that key tells what the setting is and its value now. The object, when named, narrows where; with none it is about the plate or the setup. count says how many warnings there are; read slice_report's findings when more than the first matters. An ignored one is a finding the person chose not to be told about again: still true of the slice. Explain a finding from its words, never from a cause you supply.

A warning is my statement about the slice, not proof the print will fail. Say what it risks for this print and its purpose. Some are the person's call because they trade the look, the time or their hardware: adding support (marks on the surface, clean-up), re-orienting, a filament pairing, a nozzle. A setting that only shapes the toolpath is yours to settle when the request covers it.

A finding counts as resolved only when a new slice no longer reports it, never because a setting changed or a chip was closed or ignored. Asked whether the print is ready, name what the slice still warns about.

| What I report while slicing | What it usually means, and where it points |
| --- | --- |
| "It seems object … has floating regions / floating cantilever / large overhangs. Please re-orient the object or enable support generation."; "Your model needs support!" | Parts start in the air or overhang far and will sag or fail without support. Support settings (enable_support, support_type) or orientation; which one is the person's call. |
| "Object can't be printed for empty layer between … and …" (critical) | Layers with nothing printed: features thinner than a line, or a broken mesh. object_analyze, object_repair, layer height or line widths. |
| "… is too close to others, and collisions may be caused."; "Prime Tower is too close to others"; "too close to exclusion area" | The nozzle or head may hit an object, the tower or a no-go area. Position (object_place, plate_layout) or print_sequence. |
| "Found gcode path conflicts between object … and …" (critical) | Two objects' paths cross. Spacing or layout. |
| "A G-code path goes beyond the plate boundaries." / "… beyond the max print height." | A skirt, brim, support or the object itself leaves the printable area by a little (more is a blocker). Position, brim_width, skirt_distance or size. |
| Speed, acceleration, jerk or junction deviation above the printer's maximum ("Orca will automatically cap …"); "Setting the jerk speed too low …" | It prints with the motion capped to the printer's limits. The setting named, or the printer's machine_max_* values. |
| A support base pattern replaced ("Rectilinear will be used instead") | I substitute a pattern this support type cannot use. support_base_pattern. |
| "Partial flushing volume set to 0 …"; "PLA and PETG filaments detected in the mixture …"; filament shrinkage or XY size compensation "will not be used"; different nozzle and filament diameters with the prime tower | Multi-filament settings: colours may mix, or a setting is dropped for this plate. Flushing volumes, the filaments chosen, the setting named. |
| "The nozzle hardness required by the filament is higher than …" | An abrasive filament wears the installed nozzle. Physical, the person's call: nozzle or filament. |
| Traditional timelapse "may cause surface imperfections"; smooth timelapse with the prime tower off | Only for a print that records a timelapse. timelapse_type, enable_prime_tower. |

I raise no slicing warning for thin walls, bridges, bed adhesion, brims or cooling. When the person asks about those, read slice_report's firstLayer, islands and supports sections and the settings; never present one as a warning I gave.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One step of the project chat against the live model, without the app.

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt (projectInstructions.ts), the
project tools and the chat. Each case here is one point in a project chat,
recorded from the real app, and the model's next step there, a tool call or a
reply, checked against one sentence of the prompt. A response may hold
several calls, and every one is judged: a change among them is the outcome
and ends the run, whatever came before it. A response of reads the case does
not decide on is answered, each read with the result the app gave for it at
the same point (recorded beside the request), and the model asked again, at
most MAX_READS times; nothing else is ever answered.

What the app sends, reproduced here:
  - instructions: rendered from projectInstructions.ts by
    tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs, so an edit to the prompt is tested
    without building anything;
  - tools: project_tools.json, the app's own tool list for the project chat
    (test_openai_responses_agent.cpp fails if it drifts from the registry);
  - input: everything else, as the app built it (requests.json). The shell
    harness's --project-prompt-requests mode plays script.json through the
    real app, with the model's outputs scripted and every tool run for real,
    and keeps the request at each point a case observes: the earlier turns as
    the app replays them, this turn's message with the workspace context, and
    this turn's calls with their live results. At the same point it calls

    setting of the print, the first object, the filament and the printer,
    the filament's and printer's names asked under the print scope, a
    hand-kept list of other slicers' names, and settings_search for common
    queries) and keeps
    their results: those are the only answers a read can get.
The app streams its requests; this script does not. Nothing else differs,
except which model answers them.

(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it

Add the print-issues skill and a per-plate summary of slice warnings

A third app-triggered skill for the project chat, print-issues (trigger
print_issues, AgentUI/src/skills/print-issues/SKILL.md, 4,597 bytes of text).
It holds what the two buttons on a print-issue chip ask for, moved out of the
standing prompt with its "and only that" scope; how to read a finding (severity,
setting key, object); that a warning is the app's statement about the slice,
not proof of failure, and which calls are the person's; that a finding is
resolved only when a new slice no longer reports it; and a table of the warning
families OrcaSlicer raises while slicing, in its own words, found in libslic3r
and the notifications NoticeKinds routes. It also says OrcaSlicer raises no
slicing warning for thin walls, bridges, adhesion, brims or cooling.

The host fires it on the request that carries a chip's message (a
<print_issue> block), and on the first request whose workspace shows a plate
with slice warnings no request has carried yet: the next message after the
person's Slice, or the tool result that shows the model's own slice. A
re-slice with the same warnings fires nothing; the skill is never stored.

The fact rides on every request: each plate's sliceWarnings (count, ignored
count, and the first warning to read, critical first, with OrcaSlicer's words,
setting and object) in the <workspace> block, a tool result's workspace and the
slicing section. OrcaWorkspaceAdapter reads it from the print-issue monitor
through a reader the shell installs, refreshed at read time so a slice_start
result already has it, and keeps it per plate for as long as that slice is the
plate's own. Its sequence advances only when a slice reports a warning the
plate's last record did not. It lists what slice_report lists, so the
bed-temperature warning (1000C001) and the older-firmware timelapse copy
(1000C003) are left out.

chip request is updated for the context block of 36d33312ed. No live model
batch has been run.

# Skill 3: issues OrcaSlicer reports (print-issues)

Branch `claude/skill-print-issues`, one commit `0fb4593f1b` on local `jusprin-newui` at `1435f4c817`. Not pushed, not merged. This report is untracked on purpose.

## 1. The problem

The project chat's model had two blind spots around OrcaSlicer's own findings.

First, the two buttons on a print-issue chip on the canvas ("Ask AI" sends "Explain this issue and my options.", "Resolve with AI" sends "Help fix this issue.") were explained by one sentence in the standing prompt. The model read that sentence on every turn, though it only matters on the turn a button was pressed.

Second, when a slice finished with warnings (for example "It seems object Slab has floating cantilever. Please re-orient the object or enable support generation."), nothing told the model. The `slice_start` reply looked the same as a clean slice. The model learned of warnings only if it chose to call `slice_report` with its findings section, which is why the prompt says "check slice_report before calling a print ready". If the person pressed Slice themselves, the model was never told at all.

## 2. What changed

**The skill.** A new file, `AgentUI/src/skills/print-issues/SKILL.md`, with trigger `print_issues`. The text is 4,597 bytes; the model-arrived skill is 6,918. It opens with "The rules above still apply" and covers:
- what each chip button asks for, moved out of the prompt with its "and only that" scope;
- how to read a finding: a blocker means no slice or print until it is fixed, a warning means the slice can print. The setting key names what to change, and `settings_search` or `settings_get` says what that setting is. The object narrows where the problem is;
- that a warning is the app's statement about the slice, not proof the print will fail, and which choices belong to the person (support marks, orientation, filament pairing, nozzle);
- that a finding is resolved only when a new slice no longer reports it, not when a setting changes or a chip is closed or ignored;
- a table of the warning families OrcaSlicer raises while slicing, quoting its real messages from `libslic3r` (step warnings, `Print::validate` warnings, slice-result warnings) and the notification kinds `NoticeKinds.cpp` routes. The families are: support needed, empty layers, collisions, path conflicts, paths off the plate, capped motion limits, replaced support patterns, multi-filament and purge, nozzle hardness, and timelapse.

The brief asked for thin walls, bridging, bed adhesion, brims and cooling too. OrcaSlicer raises no slicing warning for any of them, so the skill says so and points to `slice_report`'s sections instead of inventing messages.

**When it fires.** `AgentHost::fire_print_issues` adds the skill as the last item of:
- the request that carries a chip's message (the message has a `<print_issue>` block);
- the first request whose workspace shows a plate with warnings no request has carried yet. After the person's Slice, that is their next message. After the model's own slice, it is the tool result that shows the warnings (the `slice_start` reply when it waited).

A re-slice that reports the same warnings fires nothing. When a slice reports a warning the plate's last slice did not have, it fires again. The skill is never stored, and the next request does not carry it.

**The fact.** Every request now carries each plate's `sliceWarnings` in three places: the `<workspace>` block, a tool result's workspace, and the slicing section of `workspace_inspect` and `slice_start`. It holds the count, how many the person ignored, and the first warning to read (critical ones first), in OrcaSlicer's words with its setting and object. `slice_report` still has the full list.

The workspace adapter reads this from the print-issue monitor through a reader the shell installs. It keeps the summary per plate for as long as that slice is still the plate's current one. It counts the same warnings `slice_report` lists, so it leaves out the bed-temperature warning (code `1000C001`) and a duplicate timelapse warning (`1000C003`). See Remaining issues for why.

**The prompt** loses the print-issue bullet: 2,364 to 2,195 bytes. `workspace_inspect`'s description now mentions the warnings, and `project_tools.json` is regenerated.

**The eval.** `issue-fix` and `issue-explain` are re-pointed to the skill. A new case, `slice-warnings-ready`, covers the overhang fixture sliced by the person, then "is this good to print?". It passes on a `slice_report` read, or on a reply that names the warning as the app's own and recommends what to do. It fails on any change, or on calling the print ready without the warning. The recorder now checks any page skill (`"skill": "print-issues"`), checks that no other point carries a skill, and checks that the next request does not carry it. `requests.json` is re-recorded.

**Size.** 885 lines added and 61 removed, not counting `requests.json`, which has 4,193 lines added and 1,023 removed.

## 3. Tests and results

All of these were run on this branch's final build (Release):

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `agent_bridge_tests` | 316 cases pass |
| `jusprin_tests` | 113 cases pass |
| `workspace_contract_tests` | 42 cases pass |
| Real-adapter workspace harness | pass, 5,945 checks |
| Shell harness, default scenario | pass, 550 checks |
| Shell harness `--print-issues` | pass, 0 failures |
| AgentUI vitest | 429 tests pass |
| `test_steps.py` | 18 tests pass |
| `run_prompt_tests.py --render-only` | 21 cases render |
| Recorder, `--project-prompt-requests` | pass, 6,724 checks |

The `jusprin_web` bundle was rebuilt before vitest and the recording.

New tests:
- Host tests: the skill on a chip's request, after the person's slice, and after the model's own `slice_start` with wait. Also: no skill on a clean slice, none on any later request, and none for a re-slice with the same warnings. Plus the summary JSON, present and absent.
- PrintIssue tests: which warnings count, the excluded codes, the summary rule, and when warnings count as new.
- Page tests: the skill's content, and that the prompt no longer has the button sentences.

I proved the host tests catch a broken change. With the firing and the summary output disabled, five of them failed; with the code restored, all pass.

In the real app (`--print-issues`), the overhang slice gives "It seems object issues-overhang.stl has floating cantilever…" with its object. The summary is present at the first workspace change that shows the plate sliced. The chip's request carries the skill.

That timing check failed at first, because the monitor had not re-read OrcaSlicer yet. The reader now refreshes the monitor before reading. Its callbacks only redraw the overlay and post chat entries; they never read the workspace.

In the recording, the skill sits on `issue-fix`, `issue-explain` and `slice-warnings-ready`, and on no other point. Before the bed-temperature exclusion, 6 points that should carry nothing carried the skill: every conversation on the Textured PEI Plate had that warning.

I also fixed one existing check in `--print-issues`. `ask_request_gives_the_model_the_structured_context` had been stale since 36d33312ed, which moved the issue context out of the message text into its own block. It would have failed without my change. It now checks the context block and the skill.

## 4. Remaining issues

- **Joining with skill 2 (slice failed).** The sibling's work, branch `claude/skill-slice-failed` in worktree `cool-bardeen-7f40f5`, was uncommitted when I started, so I could not build on it. I matched its shape instead. Its `WorkspacePlate::slice_failure` (a `SliceFailure` with severity, message, setting, code, object, sequence) sits next to my `slice_warnings` (a `SliceWarnings` with the same fields plus count and ignored). Its host side keeps `m_slice_failures_told` beside my `m_slice_warnings_told`, and `fire_on_new_slice_failure` beside `fire_print_issues`. Expect conflicts in these places:
  - `Workspace.hpp`;
  - the plate JSON in `AgentHost::context_json`, `OpenAIResponsesAgent::workspace_json` and `slicing_section_result`;
  - the `slicing_plate` schema;
  - `SkillTrigger`;
  - the same sentence of `workspace_inspect`'s description (merge it to "whether each plate's slice is current, what it warned about and why its last slice did not succeed");
  - `skills.test.ts`'s skill list;
  - the recorder's skill checks: its `prompt_is_any_skill` must also know `slice-failed`.

  A later cleanup could make both records one shared finding type. I left that alone.
- **The prompt's "check slice_report (slice_inspect when needed)".** The warnings part of that sentence is now redundant: the warnings reach the model without a call. The rest is not. The sentence also asks the model to check the slice against the person's requirements (time, weight, cost, supports). I left it for the main session's final prompt edit.
- **The bed-temperature warning is left out.** The chip still shows it, but the summary does not count it, to match `slice_report`, which leaves it out as OrcaSlicer's send dialog does. That means a chip can show a warning the model is not told about. Whether that warning should reach the model is your call.
- **Small edges, not fixed:**
  - If the request that first carries new warnings fails and is retried, the retry does not carry the skill (the warnings already count as told). A chip's retry does carry it.
  - The told list is per app run, not per chat, so a new chat opened after the warnings were told gets the fact but not the skill.
  - Only the active plate is read, because OrcaSlicer checks only the active plate. Another plate keeps what was read while it was active.
- **`first-person`** still starts after the scripted `slice_report`. The skill sits on the request before it, so that case still tests the prompt's first-person rule, not the skill.
- **Proposed live batch (not run).** Cases `issue-fix`, `issue-explain`, `slice-warnings-ready` and `first-person`, 3 runs each: 12 runs. By the README's last comparable batch (12 runs, 35 requests, 398,836 input tokens), expect about 35 requests, roughly 400,000 input tokens (about 70% cached), about 10,000 output tokens, and up to 9 judge calls.

import re,subprocess
files=[f for f in subprocess.check_output(['git','diff','--name-only','--diff-filter=U']).decode().split() if not f.endswith('requests.json')]
pat=re.compile(r'<<<<<<< [^\n]*\n(.*?)\|\|\|\|\|\|\| [^\n]*\n(.*?)=======\n(.*?)>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n',re.S)
ren=[('The first skill is `model-opened-or-imported` (trigger `model_arrived`): the first message after a model arrives','The first skill is `file-loaded` (trigger `file_loaded`): the first message after a file is opened or imported'),
('''// A model reached the project: the person opened or dropped a file, or a
// tool call opened or imported one.
inline constexpr const char* kModelArrived = "model_arrived";''','''// A file was opened or imported: the person opened or dropped one, or a
// tool call of the in-app Agent opened or imported one.
inline constexpr const char* kFileLoaded = "file_loaded";'''),
('kPromptArrivalSkill','kPromptFileLoadedSkill'),('kTestArrivalSkill','kTestFileLoadedSkill'),('arrival_text','file_loaded_text'),
('model-opened-or-imported','file-loaded'),('model_arrived','file_loaded'),('kModelArrived','kFileLoaded'),
('the model-arrived skill','the file-loaded skill'),('The arrival skill is the one','The file-loaded skill is the one'),
('after the plate\'s picture for an arrived model','after the plate\'s picture for a loaded file')]
for f in files:
    s=open(f).read()
    s,n=pat.subn(lambda m:m.group(3),s)
    for a,b in ren: s=s.replace(a,b)
    assert '<<<<<<<' not in s and '>>>>>>>' not in s, f
    open(f,'w').write(s); print(f,n)
EOF
